Re-stamped 27 August 2026 for §13 row 29, the maximum tolerable fixed cost, and for no other reason: max_tolerable_fixed_cost_bps = 10.0 basis points of position, round trip, excluding spread and market impact. It enters the parameter object because it decides which names exist: it is the one free parameter the clip-floor derivation cannot eliminate, and two runs under one hash could otherwise size against two tolerances and admit two universes. BOTH ENDS OF THE RANGE ARE DERIVED. Below 2.375 bp the proportional term 104/p exceeds the tolerance at the calibration share price and no position size of any kind reaches it. Above 12.5 bp the tolerance permits a trade whose fixed cost alone exceeds the 12.5 bp basis on which §5.2.2's cheapest break-even of 22.5 bp was computed at a £6.25 round trip on £5,000 notional. The withdrawn implicit rule set the clip where fixed costs fell below 25 bp, which is DOUBLE that basis and was never coherent. THE COST, STATED FIRST. 10 bp is a US-ONLY DECISION. UK Main Market is excluded with certainty, stamp duty alone being 50 bp. AIM is excluded at about 10.3 bp and NOT because of stamp duty: IBKR's UK commission is 0.05% a side, which is 10 bp round trip on its own, so the deferred AIM growth-market tier cannot rescue the UK because AIM fails on commission and not on tax. 12.5 bp is the value at which AIM becomes reachable, so the choice between 10 and 12.5 is the choice of whether the UK exists in this strategy; 10 was taken because it sits inside the range rather than at its edge. delta (50 bps), n_min (30), ratio (1.0) and seed (20260826) are carried across unchanged from the 26 August commitment, which was made before any archive exists and is therefore still blind.
